records.source: Ordinary lasso penalises each guide on its own, so from a gene's four correlated guides it keeps whichever one happens to fit best and drops the rest -- which reads as "one guide works and three do not" when the four guides are four measurements of the same gene. Group lasso penalises the gene's guides as a block:
records.translation: Vanlig lasso straffar varje guide för sig, så av en gens fyra korrelerade guider behåller den den som råkar passa bäst och tar bort resten -- vilket läses som "one guide works and three do not" när de fyra guiderna är fyra mätningar av samma gen. records.source: For a CRISPR screen it is the penalised analogue of the mixed model with random effects -- "which genes are involved, where each gene is measured by several guides" -- and it addresses that question with no random effects, no REML fit, and no `gene_fraction` column. `gene_fraction` is the sum of a gene's guide fractions, so a design carrying both blocks is singular by construction. Here the gene enters as a grouping of the guide columns, never as a column of its own, so the design stays full rank.
records.translation: För en CRISPR-screen är det den straffade motsvarigheten till den blandade modellen med slumpmässiga effekter -- "which genes are involved, where each gene is measured by several guides" -- och den besvarar den frågan utan slumpmässiga effekter, utan REML-anpassning och utan kolumnen `gene_fraction`. `gene_fraction` är summan av en gens guideandelar, så en design som bär båda blocken är till sin konstruktion singulär.
